tests.justification: This test verifies left-to-right evaluation for operators of equal precedence (subtraction). The expression 3 - 5 - 2 must evaluate as (3 - 5) - 2 = -2 - 2 = -4, not 3 - (5 - 2) = 3 - 3 = 0. This directly tests the requirement to evaluate equal-precedence operators left to right.

This test verifies left-to-right evaluation for division operators of equal precedence. The expression 10 / 2 / 5 must evaluate as (10 / 2) / 5 = 5 / 5 = 1, not 10 / (2 / 5) = 10 / 0.4 = 25. This confirms the left-to-right rule for division, which has the same precedence as multiplication.

rationale: The requirement explicitly mandates left-to-right evaluation for operators of equal precedence. These two tests cover subtraction and division, both with equal precedence, to ensure the calculator respects the left-to-right order. The expressions use only valid, well-formed syntax with nonnegative integers and terminating decimal results as per the specification.
